raw_response:
I'm 73 this year, and my back isn't getting any younger. I've farmed these fields in Quzhou for more than fifty years, so I know what my land can and can't do. I still work 5 mu myself — my son took over another plot, but I keep this piece because it gives me purpose and a little income. I'm not changing anything this year. Winter wheat is already in the ground from last October, planted with improved seed I bought at the county supply store — the same variety most of my neighbors grow. Come spring, I'll topdress with urea and irrigate three times. The electricity for the pump costs more every year, but if I don't water, the wheat will wither in this dry plain. For fertilizer, I'll spread compound fertilizer before planting and topdress later — altogether about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu for the wheat. I can't afford to waste money since my savings are thin, but I've learned the hard way that cutting too much on fertilizer means small ears and empty pockets at harvest. After we harvest the wheat in early June, I'll hire the custom operator to plant hybrid maize right behind the combine using a no-till planter. I'm too old to be turning soil by hand in that summer heat, and besides, the window between crops is barely a week. Two sprays for the corn — one for weeds, one for the corn borer. I expect about 400 kg per mu from the wheat and 480 kg per mu from the maize. Not the highest in the village, but steady, and at my age steady is better than sorry.
